answer: Recursive Flow Constriction Protocol Nodes calculate incoming trust value through independent upstream routing paths. If multiple local identities share an excessive volume of identical intermediate hops, the network treats them as a single cluster facing a data gale. An attacker trying to flood the system must then forge redundant connection routes across distant network regions. This forces the adversary to pay a heavy computational penalty by maintaining high-latency links, degrading sybil efficiency as the local topology horizon expands.
